free_aliases._sources: Spellings of one model that the free-group stripping (free_canonical in sync.py) does not unify, for the free/<model> groups only. Evidence: models.dev (https://models.dev/api.json, fetched 2026-11-26) names them one model: 'Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B' (family nemotron-lightning) for nemotron-3.5-lightning and nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b; 'Beam 1.0 501B A23B' for beam, beam-1.0 and beam-1.0-501b-a23b; 'Gemma 4 31B IT' for gemma-4-31b and gemma-4-31b-it.

paid_only._source: Models a free route's provider says need a paid plan: never free, never probed, never deployed, whatever the listing shows. Cloudflare: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/ (read 2026-11-26): 'Some models require a paid billing method. This applies to' the ids below; 'You can access these models with either the Workers Paid plan or prepaid AI Gateway credits.' The /ai/models/search listing the sync reads has no documented field for this (the limits page says each model page states it), so the list is kept here and checked by hand when the pricing page changes.

reference._sources: models.dev (https://models.dev/api.json, fetched 2026-11-26): route -> its provider id there. Matched by model id inside that provider only: modalities, type, status (deprecated) and cost (per million tokens, 0 is free). Measured coverage of the ids each route lists: kilo 459 of 464, groq 11 of 11, zai 15 of 16, ovh 19 of 33, google 36 of 65, opencode-go 18 of 24, nvidia 13 of 30, unorouter 13 of 311, requesty 177 models in models.dev (spelled differently from the route's), vibe 26 of 63. Naga, Routeway and Inferbase are not in models.dev: their own listings carry kinds, availability, price and dates (Naga, Routeway) or nothing (Inferbase). OpenRouter is left out on purpose.

free_order._note: Order inside a free/<model> group, lowest first: the per-minute providers before the scarce daily and monthly allowances, so a daily budget is spent only when the per-minute ones are limited. config/free_limits.py removes a limited copy before the pick, so order is preference, not a wait. A route not named comes last.

free_limits._note: Per free route: `deployment` is copied into each deployment's litellm_params (LiteLLM 1.109.1 enforces rpm, tpm, rpd, tpd and max_parallel_requests per deployment with enforce_model_rate_limits; rpd/tpd reset at `reset`, HH:MM UTC, default 00:00). `shared` is a budget one provider account or IP shares across all its deployments, `concurrency` the requests in flight across the route: config/free_limits.py counts both and drops the route's deployments from the pick once spent, until the window turns. `scope` is what a learned limit (a 429, a 402, x-ratelimit-remaining 0) blocks: the one deployment (route + upstream model) or the whole account; `account_match` escalates an error whose text matches to the account. `status`: confirmed (the source states it), partial, unconfirmed (registry or route notes only). A route without an entry still learns from its 429s.

groq.source: https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits (the table is the Developer plan's base limits for gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b and qwen3.8-27b; the free plan's own numbers are in the console only). Headers: retry-after on 429, x-ratelimit-remaining/reset-requests (per day) and -tokens (per minute).

shared.note: 1000 once the account has bought 10 credits

openrouter.source: https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits: :free models 20 RPM; 50 per day under 10 credits bought, 1000 at 10 or more; one daily counter per account (current UTC day); 429 with Retry-After.

kilo.source: https://kilo.ai/docs/gateway/usage-and-billing: 200 requests per hour per IP for all free models; 429 'Rate limit exceeded for free models'. Window alignment not stated (counted per clock hour).

cloudflare.source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/limits/ (300 RPM for text generation) and /pricing/ (10,000 Neurons a day per account, all limits reset 00:00 UTC). Neurons per request vary, so the daily allowance is learned from the 429, not counted.

zai.source: https://docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing states GLM-4.7-Flash, GLM-4.5-Flash and GLM-4.6V-Flash free; no rate limit is published (the rate-limits page answers 404). One request in flight is the route's earlier note.

poe.source: https://creator.poe.com/docs/external-applications/openai-compatible-api: 500 RPM, x-ratelimit-*-requests headers, Retry-After on 429. API calls spend points. The account has no subscription or payment method (owner, 2026-11-26), so only its free daily points can be spent: free and rate limited, a spent allowance is refused (402 or 429, which blocks the account until the daily reset).

requesty.source: provider registry: 200 requests a day and 20 a minute shared across the free models.

routeway.source: provider registry: 200 requests a day, one in flight, low priority.

ovh.source: sync.py note: 2 requests a minute per IP per model.

bazaarlink.source: provider registry: 10 RPM, 60 weighted units a day, 2 concurrent (no credit), reset 00:00 UTC.

plugsky.source: https://plugsky.com/pricing and https://plugsky.com/models (read 2026-11-26): the Free plan serves plugsky-micro and plugsky-lite only; 30 RPM, 1 concurrent, 100 requests and 50K tokens a day for accounts from 2 Nov 2026 (the Free section also speaks of a rolling 5-hour window; which is enforced is not stated).

cohere.source: provider registry: trial key, 1,000 calls a month, 20 RPM per chat model.

unorouter.source: route notes: anonymous, queue-throttled about one a minute per model per IP.

google.source: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/rate-limits: limits per project, RPD resets at midnight Pacific (08:00 UTC in winter; 07:00 in summer, so 08:00 is the later, safe one). Per-model RPM/RPD are shown in AI Studio only (https://aistudio.google.com/rate-limit), not on a public page, so they are learned from the 429s. The key's project has no billing account (owner, 2026-11-26): a model the free tier does not serve answers 429 or 403 and is blocked, never billed.

nvidia.source: build.nvidia.com (NVIDIA Developer Program, hosted NIM for prototyping): 40 requests a minute per account is the commonly stated limit; no NVIDIA page read on 2026-11-26 states the limit, credits or paid models (build.nvidia.com/faq answers 404). A 402 or a credit error blocks the account.

inferbase.source: The account has no payment method (owner, 2026-11-26): its daily dollar allowance is the limit, learned from the refusal (402 or a quota error blocks the account until the daily reset).

vercel.source: provider registry: monthly free credits; 429 over the limit, 402 with no balance (learned, not counted).
